title: Rava bar Zimuna
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: What remains for us from him is his precious saying, which is stated in Shabbat 112b: Rabbi Zeira said that Rava bar Zimuna said: If the earlier ones were like angels, we are like human beings; and if the earlier ones were like human beings, we are like donkeys, etc.
The saying is repeated in Shekalim, beginning of chapter 5: Rabbi Abba Zemina, in the name of Rabbi Zeira: “If the earlier ones were angels,” etc.

In Jerusalem Talmud Demai 1:3, the reading is “Rabbi Abba bar Zavina (it should read Zemina) said in the name of Rabbi Zeira.” Hyman explains the difference by saying that he was the first Rabbi Zeira’s student and the second Rabbi Zeira’s teacher: in the Bavli, the second Rabbi Zeira reported in his name; in the Jerusalem Talmud, he reported in the first Rabbi Zeira’s name.

notes.text: Hyman distinguishes two Rabbi Zeiras: the subject was the first’s student and the second’s teacher. These are his historical explanation of the opposite attribution directions.

The consulted Shabbat 112b has Rabbi Zeira reporting Rava bar Zimuna. The opposite reporting direction in the supplied Palestinian parallels, correction Zavina/Zemina and explanation through two Rabbi Zeiras remain Hyman’s reconstruction, not a new identity merger.
